declared_model.clock_one: scalar phi, with FP_phi={phi,C}>0 on the declared component
declared_model.clock_two: geometric trace momentum P, with FP_P={P,C}=-C_Q>0 on shell
declared_model.failed_control_clock: Q=2 log(a), whose FP factor {Q,C}=C_P vanishes at P=0 and changes sign

exact_checks.statement: C=0 is equivalent to exp(-3Q/2)R=72*pi^4*exp(Q/2), hence exp(2Q)=R/(72*pi^4).
The on-shell coordinate Phi obeys {Phi,C}=3p C/(2R) and is therefore weakly Dirac on R>0.
The scalar momentum p strongly commutes with C.
The exact identity {P,C}=12*pi^2*exp(Q/2)+3C/2 makes the P-clock FP factor positive on shell.
The Q-clock FP factor is -exp(-3Q/2)P/(3*pi^2), so it vanishes and changes sign at P=0.
The scalar-clock complete observable P_phi(tau) returns P at tau=phi.
The scalar-clock complete observable Q_phi(tau) returns the on-shell Q at tau=phi.
The P-clock complete observable phi_P(sigma) returns phi at sigma=P.
The P-clock complete observable Q_P(sigma) returns the on-shell Q at sigma=P.
The two clock descriptions assign the same Q on their common chart.
For p>0, d P_phi/d tau=p sech^2(...) is strictly positive.
For |sigma|<sqrt(3/2)p, d phi_P/d sigma is strictly positive.
The scalar clock covers the orbit with R=3p^2 sech^2(...)>0 for every finite tau.
Every smooth complete observable written only in Phi, p and an external clock reading weakly commutes with C on this chart.

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: phi is a global classical clock on the declared open orbit; no statement is made at the singular R=0 ends or in another component
theorem_guards.hypotheses: p>0 makes {phi,C}>0 and P_phi(tau) maps every finite real tau into |P|<sqrt(3/2)p

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: P is a valid geometric clock on the finite open interval and its complete observables are inverse to the scalar-clock chart there
theorem_guards.hypotheses: on C=0, {P,C}=12*pi^2 exp(Q/2)>0 and sigma is restricted to |sigma|<sqrt(3/2)p
theorem_guards.theorem: inverse function theorem on a monotone gauge orbit

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: atanh(tanh u)=u and tanh(atanh x)=x on the declared real principal branches; this supplies the second inverse composition without analytic continuation
theorem_guards.hypotheses: all arguments sqrt(2/3)sigma/p lie in (-1,1) and all scalar-clock parameters are real
theorem_guards.theorem: real inverse relation between tanh and atanh

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: Q cannot be one global clock across the maximal-scale turning point; two branch charts would be extra data, not a failure of the constrained dynamics
theorem_guards.hypotheses: {Q,C} vanishes at P=0 and has opposite signs on P<0 and P>0

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: classical overlap agreement does not imply a unitary quantum clock-change map, equal self-adjoint domains, or clock-independent quantum probabilities
